newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama Canal improvements to be completed by 2002.
newsitem.headline: Panama Canal improvements to be completed by 2002.

text.p: Most of the Panama Canal's 10-year, $3-billion expansion and maintenance program will be completed ahead of schedule by the year 2002, canal administrator Alberto Aleman Zubieta said.
"Most of the projects will be finished by 2002. The widening of Gaillard Cut will be finished 10 years ahead of time by 2002," he told Reuters in an interview.
"We're putting new technology to the canal to make it more efficient and responsive to client needs," he said.
Panama is to regain control of the world's busiest waterway in the year 2000.
The widening of Gaillard Cut, the narrowest point in the 52-mile transoceanic waterway, is the largest project.

The cut will be widened from 500 feet (154 meters) at its narrowest point to 630 feet (194 meters) to allow 24-hour passage of the large 100-foot (31-meter) Panamax ships. Currently, Panamax ships pass through only during day-time hours.
The Panama Canal Commission (PCC) recently approved a two- step toll increase to help pay for the improvements.
The general toll rate will rise 8.2 percent as of January 1, 1997 and 7.5 percent January 1, 1998. There will also be a charge for on-deck container space.

Aleman said other projects such as a computerized traffic management system to track every ship that entered the canal should be in place before the end of the century and all the locks should be fully hydraulic by 2005. "All of this will lead to less time ships will have to wait in canal waters."
PCC officials, he said, are not concerned about Nicaragua's proposal to build a "dry canal" rail system to transport container cargo across the Central American isthmus.
"We understand there is competition. Panama already has a water and dry canal. The market will dictate whether those schemes will be a reality or not," he said.

He added that the privatization of Cristobal port on the Atlantic coast and Balboa port on the Pacific, the canal's points of entry, "will make Panama a hub for containerized cargo, which will be beneficial to the canal."
